Official English EUR-Lex text and instrument identity reviewed on 2026-10-23; the Czech official route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. This amending act is not a consolidated Visa Code. Article 8(2) makes general application depend on the Commission decision under Article 7(1), with exceptions in Article 8(3). Verify the decision and any Czech notification before describing the EU Visa Application Platform as operational. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

Official English EUR-Lex text and instrument identity reviewed on 2026-10-23; the Czech official route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 covers identity cards and residence documents under Directive 2004/38, with EEA relevance. The 3 August 2026 transition date has passed; check Article 8 and the actual document before assessing validity. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

Official English text and instrument identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. This amending act changes the uniform visa format to a digital format, but Article 3 defers general application to a Commission implementing decision under Article 2(1), with a limited exception for Article 1 point 2 from 27 December 2023. Check the decision in the Official Journal before describing digital visas as operational. This is not a consolidated text of Regulation (EC) No 1683/95. The Czech official route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

The official English text and Article 2 scope were reviewed on 2026-10-23. It covers specified Member-State public documents, including marriage and parentage records; Article 2(3) excludes third-country public documents and Article 2(4) excludes recognition of the legal effects of another Member State's document. The Czech official route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

EUR-Lex identifies the current consolidated version dated 12 June 2026. Article 2(1)(c) covers visa-exempt third-country family members of Union citizens or equivalent free-movement beneficiaries who lack the specified residence card or permit; Article 2(2)(b)-(c) excludes qualifying cardholders. On 2026-10-23 the official ETIAS FAQ said the system was not operating and no applications were being collected; the Commission scheduled launch for Q4 2026 without an exact date. Recheck official operational status and the actual residence document before applying. The Czech official route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Official Journal act published 15 June 2022; in force and applicable from 1 October 2022; EUR-Lex displayed no consolidated version on 23 October 2026. Scope: Peer evaluation and monitoring of application of the Schengen acquis, including visas, external borders, return, information systems, agency and private-service activities, and fundamental-rights safeguards. Limitations: This is an oversight/evaluation mechanism, not an individual complaint or appeal procedure; evaluation reports may be restricted. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. Scope: European Border and Coast Guard/Frontex mandate, joint operations, standing corps, fundamental-rights oversight and complaints, and Member-State responsibilities. Limitations: This does not set individual visa or residence-card eligibility rules. Review related implementing measures and national responsibilities for the issue at hand. External-only reference; no local copy or country-topic coverage/completion is implied.

Official EUR-Lex record and source identity reviewed on 2026-10-23. EUR-Lex current consolidated version dated 8 January 2025, corrected by Corrigendum OJ L 90502 of 17 June 2025.
